items.description: Analyze repository structure and initialize project skeleton
items.acceptance_criteria: Create a well-organized project directory structure with: src/ for source code, tests/ for test suite, benchmarks/ for benchmark scripts, data/ for test grids, docs/ for documentation. Include a pyproject.toml or requirements.txt with numpy, pytest, and matplotlib as minimum dependencies. Document the project layout in a STRUCTURE.md file listing each directory and its purpose.
items.notes: Project skeleton created with src/, tests/, benchmarks/, data/, results/, figures/, docs/ directories. requirements.txt with numpy, pytest, matplotlib, seaborn, pytest-cov. STRUCTURE.md documents layout.

items.description: Literature review of classic voxel grid traversal algorithms (DDA, Amanatides-Woo, Bresenham 3D)
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce a literature_review.md document covering: (1) Amanatides & Woo 1987 DDA algorithm with pseudocode analysis, (2) 3D Bresenham line algorithm and its voxel traversal variant, (3) Cleary & Wyvill supercover algorithm, (4) Siddon's algorithm for radiological path computation. Each algorithm must include time complexity, per-step operation count, and known limitations. At least 5 papers cited with BibTeX entries added to sources.bib.
items.notes: Literature review covers Amanatides-Woo DDA, 3D Bresenham, Cleary-Wyvill, Siddon algorithms with pseudocode, complexity, limitations. 5 BibTeX entries in sources.bib.

items.description: Literature review of hierarchical and acceleration-structure-based voxel traversal methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Extend literature_review.md with coverage of: (1) Sparse Voxel Octrees (Laine & Karras 2010), (2) Sparse 64-trees and brickmap approaches (dubiousconst282, 2024), (3) ESVO traversal and its limitations, (4) Multi-resolution voxel grids with spatial hashing, (5) Octree-R cost-optimized partitioning. Each method must include asymptotic complexity analysis and space-time tradeoff discussion. At least 5 additional papers cited in sources.bib (cumulative >=10).
items.notes: Extended literature review with SVO (Laine-Karras), Sparse 64-trees, Sparse Voxel DAGs, spatial hashing, Octree-R. 6 new BibTeX entries (cumulative 11). Includes complexity analysis and space-time tradeoffs.

items.description: Survey SIMD, GPU, and branchless optimization techniques for voxel traversal
items.acceptance_criteria: Extend literature_review.md with: (1) Es & Isler 2007 GPU-mapped grid traversal, (2) Friederichs 2025 axis-normalized ray-box intersection with SIMD, (3) branchless DDA implementations and their performance characteristics, (4) MultiDDA and XBrickMap bitmask-based hierarchical skipping (VoxelRT project), (5) cache-aware and memory-layout optimizations (Morton/Z-order curves, Hilbert curves). At least 3 additional papers cited in sources.bib (cumulative >=13).
items.notes: Added Section 3 to literature review covering: GPU-mapped traversal (Es & Isler 2007), branchless DDA, axis-normalized SIMD ray-box intersection, MultiDDA/XBrickMap bitmask skipping, Morton/Hilbert cache layouts. 4 new BibTeX entries (cumulative 15).

items.description: Survey open-source voxel traversal implementations, benchmarks, and datasets
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in literature_review.md at least 5 open-source implementations: (1) cgyurgyik/fast-voxel-traversal-algorithm, (2) francisengelmann/fast_voxel_traversal, (3) dubiousconst282/VoxelRT, (4) OpenVDB/NanoVDB traversal utilities, (5) any additional relevant repos. For each, note language, algorithmic approach, grid size limits, and reported performance. Identify at least 2 standard benchmark scenarios or datasets used in the literature.
items.notes: Documented 5 open-source implementations (cgyurgyik, engelmann, VoxelRT, OpenVDB/NanoVDB, risteon). Identified 2 standard benchmark scenarios. Cross-domain connection to medical imaging documented.

items.description: Create and validate sources.bib with comprehensive BibTeX entries
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib exists in the repo root with valid BibTeX entries for all consulted sources. At least 15 relevant references covering: classic algorithms (Amanatides-Woo, Bresenham, Siddon), hierarchical methods (SVOs, octrees), modern optimizations (SIMD, branchless, bitmask), and application domains (ray tracing, medical imaging, voxel engines). Each entry must have author, title, year, and venue/journal fields. Verify parsability with a BibTeX validation check.
items.notes: sources.bib has 18 valid BibTeX entries covering classic algorithms, hierarchical methods, modern optimizations, and application domains. Validated parsability.

items.description: Implement voxel grid data structure, ray representation, and test grid generators
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/: (1) VoxelGrid class supporting arbitrary NxNxN grids (at least up to 512^3) with O(1) voxel access, storing occupancy as a compact boolean/uint8 array, (2) Ray class with origin, direction, and parameterized point evaluation, (3) grid generator functions producing: empty grid, fully occupied grid, random occupancy at configurable density, sphere shell, and axis-aligned planes. All classes must have unit tests in tests/ with >=95% line coverage on these modules.

items.description: Implement Amanatides-Woo DDA baseline voxel traversal
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement the Amanatides & Woo (1987) DDA traversal algorithm in src/traversal/dda.py (or equivalent). The function must: (1) accept a VoxelGrid and Ray, (2) return an ordered list of (voxel_index, t_enter, t_exit) tuples for all voxels intersected, (3) handle all 26 directional octants correctly including axis-aligned rays, (4) pass correctness tests verifying against known analytical ray-grid intersections for at least 10 test cases covering edge cases (axis-aligned, diagonal, corner-grazing rays).

items.description: Implement 3D Bresenham-based voxel traversal baseline
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement a 3D Bresenham/supercover voxel traversal in src/traversal/bresenham.py. The function must: (1) enumerate all voxels intersected by a line segment between two 3D points, (2) guarantee 6-connected or 26-connected traversal (configurable), (3) pass correctness tests verifying it visits all voxels that the true geometric line passes through (supercover property), with at least 8 test cases.

items.description: Implement performance benchmarking harness and evaluation metrics
items.acceptance_criteria: Create benchmarks/harness.py with: (1) configurable grid sizes (32^3, 64^3, 128^3, 256^3, 512^3), (2) configurable ray counts (1K, 10K, 100K, 1M), (3) ray distribution generators (uniform random, coherent bundles, axis-aligned), (4) timing with sub-microsecond precision using time.perf_counter_ns or equivalent, (5) metrics computed: throughput (rays/second), average voxels traversed per ray, cache miss rate proxy (optional), memory usage. Output results as JSON for downstream analysis.

items.description: Run baseline benchmarks and establish reference performance numbers
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute the benchmarking harness on both DDA and Bresenham baselines across all grid sizes and ray distributions. Produce baseline_results.json containing: (1) throughput numbers for each (algorithm, grid_size, ray_count, distribution) combination, (2) at least 30 distinct benchmark configurations, (3) statistical summary with mean, std, min, max over 5 runs per configuration. Document baseline performance characteristics in RESULTS.md with a summary table.

items.description: Design and implement SIMD-vectorized DDA traversal using NumPy vectorization or intrinsics
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/traversal/simd_dda.py a vectorized DDA that processes batches of rays simultaneously: (1) use NumPy vectorized operations to process N rays in parallel through the same grid, (2) eliminate per-ray Python loops in the hot path - the inner traversal step must operate on arrays of ray states, (3) pass all correctness tests from item_008 (results must match scalar DDA exactly), (4) achieve at least 3x throughput improvement over scalar DDA baseline on 100K rays through a 128^3 grid.

items.description: Design and implement branchless traversal variant with minimal conditional logic
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/traversal/branchless.py a traversal algorithm that: (1) replaces conditional axis-selection branches with arithmetic operations (e.g., using argmin on tMax components or masking), (2) has at most 1 conditional branch in the inner loop (the loop termination check), (3) documents the branch elimination technique with inline comments, (4) passes all correctness tests from item_008, (5) demonstrates measurably reduced branch misprediction impact (measure via benchmarks showing improved performance on incoherent/random ray distributions compared to branching DDA).

items.description: Implement cache-aware blocked traversal with Z-order (Morton code) voxel layout
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/traversal/cache_aware.py: (1) a MortonGrid class that stores voxels in Z-order curve layout for improved spatial locality, (2) a DDA traversal adapted for the Morton-coded grid, (3) utility functions for 3D-to-Morton and Morton-to-3D index conversion, (4) correctness tests verifying identical traversal results to the standard DDA on at least 10 test cases, (5) benchmark comparison showing the cache locality impact on grids >=256^3 with documentation of observed speedup or analysis if no speedup is observed.

items.description: Implement hierarchical multi-resolution traversal with bitmask-based empty space skipping
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/traversal/hierarchical.py: (1) a two-level grid structure: coarse blocks (e.g., 8^3 bricks) with per-block occupancy bitmask and fine per-voxel traversal, (2) coarse-level DDA that skips entirely empty blocks, (3) fine-level DDA within occupied blocks, (4) correctness tests verifying identical voxel hit results to flat DDA, (5) demonstrate at least 2x speedup on sparse grids (<=25% occupancy) at 256^3 compared to flat DDA baseline. Reference the MultiDDA/XBrickMap approaches from the literature review.

items.description: Design and implement the novel hybrid adaptive traversal algorithm
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/traversal/adaptive_hybrid.py a novel algorithm that combines the best techniques from items 012-015: (1) uses hierarchical empty-space skipping at the coarse level, (2) applies branchless vectorized DDA at the fine level, (3) includes an adaptive mechanism that selects traversal strategy based on local grid density (switch between fine DDA and skip mode based on brick occupancy), (4) passes all correctness tests, (5) achieves the best overall throughput across both sparse and dense grids compared to all prior implementations. Document the algorithmic novelty and design rationale in a DESIGN.md file.

items.description: Implement coherent ray batching with shared traversal state for ray bundles
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/traversal/coherent_batch.py: (1) a ray sorting/grouping step that clusters rays by direction similarity (e.g., directional hashing into octants or finer bins), (2) shared traversal bookkeeping across coherent ray groups to amortize setup costs, (3) demonstrate improved throughput on coherent ray distributions (at least 1.5x over non-batched approaches), (4) analyze and document the tradeoff: at what coherence threshold does batching become beneficial vs. overhead-dominated.

items.description: Comprehensive benchmark of all algorithms across grid sizes 32^3 to 512^3
items.acceptance_criteria: Run full benchmark suite across all 7 traversal implementations (DDA, Bresenham, SIMD DDA, branchless, cache-aware, hierarchical, adaptive hybrid) with: (1) grid sizes 32^3, 64^3, 128^3, 256^3, 512^3, (2) ray counts 10K and 100K, (3) three ray distributions (uniform random, coherent bundles, axis-aligned), (4) three grid occupancy levels (10% sparse, 50% medium, 90% dense), (5) 5 repetitions per configuration for statistical significance. Store results in experiment_results.json with >=300 data points total.

items.description: Scaling analysis: measure throughput vs. grid size and identify algorithmic scaling behavior
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce a scaling_analysis section in RESULTS.md containing: (1) log-log plots of throughput vs grid size for each algorithm, (2) empirical scaling exponent fits (e.g., O(N^alpha) per ray where N is grid side length), (3) identification of which algorithms maintain near-constant per-ray cost vs which degrade with grid size, (4) comparison of empirical scaling against theoretical complexity from literature review. Include at least 3 plots saved as PNG files in docs/figures/.

items.description: Correctness and robustness stress tests across all implementations
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement a comprehensive correctness test suite in tests/test_correctness.py: (1) for each algorithm, verify that every reported voxel actually intersects the ray geometry (no false positives), (2) verify no voxels are missed by comparing against a brute-force reference (no false negatives) for grids up to 64^3, (3) test numerical edge cases: rays exactly on voxel boundaries, rays through grid corners, near-zero direction components, very long rays (>10000 voxels), (4) all 7 implementations pass all tests with 0 failures.

items.description: Compare novel algorithm performance against reported results in prior work
items.acceptance_criteria: In RESULTS.md, include a comparison_with_prior_work section that: (1) reproduces or references performance numbers from at least 5 papers in sources.bib (normalized to comparable metrics like voxels/second or rays/second), (2) positions the novel adaptive hybrid algorithm's performance relative to these baselines, (3) discusses where the novel approach wins and where it has limitations, (4) includes a comparison table with columns: Algorithm, Source, Grid Size, Throughput, Notes.

items.description: Sensitivity analysis: measure impact of grid occupancy density and ray coherence on each algorithm
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce a sensitivity_analysis section in RESULTS.md: (1) sweep grid occupancy from 5% to 95% in 10% increments for 128^3 grid, measuring throughput of all algorithms, (2) sweep ray coherence from fully random to perfectly coherent (at least 5 coherence levels), (3) identify crossover points where hierarchical methods overtake flat methods, (4) include at least 2 heatmap or line-plot visualizations saved in docs/figures/.

items.description: Compile comprehensive RESULTS.md with all experimental findings
items.acceptance_criteria: RESULTS.md contains: (1) executive summary of key findings in <=500 words, (2) all benchmark tables from phases 2 and 4, (3) all plots and figures referenced inline, (4) statistical significance notes (mean +/- std for all reported numbers), (5) clear identification of the fastest algorithm for each scenario category (sparse vs dense, coherent vs random, small vs large grid), (6) discussion of when to use which algorithm (practical guidance).

items.description: Write comprehensive test suite achieving >=90% code coverage
items.acceptance_criteria: tests/ directory contains: (1) unit tests for every public function in src/, (2) integration tests for end-to-end ray-grid traversal scenarios, (3) property-based tests verifying invariants (e.g., traversed voxels form a connected path, t-values are monotonically increasing), (4) total test count >= 40, (5) all tests pass, (6) code coverage >= 90% as measured by pytest-cov or equivalent.

items.description: Write comprehensive README.md with usage examples, algorithmic descriptions, and final sources.bib validation
items.acceptance_criteria: README.md contains: (1) project overview and motivation (the problem of fast voxel grid traversal), (2) installation instructions, (3) quick-start code example showing how to create a grid, cast a ray, and get traversed voxels, (4) brief description of each implemented algorithm with complexity summary, (5) benchmark summary table with the top-line result (speedup of novel approach), (6) references section citing key papers from sources.bib. Final sources.bib contains >= 15 valid BibTeX entries and parses without errors.
